answer: Give each newcomer one tidal station in a lagoon, never shared with a second identity. The holder installs a gauge ballasted with a jade weight of unique density fingerprint, then files signed tide readings in each slack-water window, each chained to the last by signature, so filings cannot be batched or replayed. Neighbors check readings against official tide tables; a copied feed fails fingerprint and table alike. One station costs $420 plus 30 calibration hours; ten thousand identities need ten thousand sites, $4,200,000, and 300,000 diver hours, no bulk purchase yields a second site.
